title: Running low / out of credits
content:
## What happens when credits run low

Emergent monitors your credit balance in real time as AI agents work on your app. **If your balance reaches zero mid-build**, the platform will pause all active generation tasks immediately. You'll see a notification in the workspace, and the build will stop wherever it left off—code already written remains saved, but the agents won't continue until you top up.

<Info title="No partial-charge surprises">
You are only charged for the work that completes. If a build stops halfway due to insufficient credits, you pay only for the tokens consumed up to that point.
</Info>

Once you **add more credits** (via the billing page or automatic renewal), you can resume the build by sending a new prompt or clicking "Continue" if the workspace offers that option. The agents will pick up context from where they stopped.

If you're uncertain how many credits remain, check the **credit balance indicator** in the top navigation bar or visit your account settings.

---

## Renewal & negative balance

Emergent supports **automatic monthly credit renewal** if you've enabled it in your billing settings. Under normal circumstances, your balance is topped up at the start of each billing cycle.

<Warning title="Negative balance and app takedown risk">
If your account has **fewer than 50 credits** at renewal time, the platform may allow your balance to go **negative** in order to complete an in-flight build. This grace period is temporary.

When Emergent's next billing check runs (typically within 24–48 hours), accounts with a negative balance will be flagged. **If the balance remains negative, your deployed app may be taken down** until you recharge and bring the account back into positive territory.
</Warning>

**To avoid this scenario:**

- Monitor your credit usage closely if you're near the end of a billing cycle.
- Set up **low-balance email alerts** (if available in your plan) so you're notified before hitting zero.
- Manually top up credits before starting a large build if your remaining balance is tight.

For more detail on how credits expire and how to recharge, see [Credit expiry & recharging](/credit-expiry-recharging).

---

## Estimating cost before building

**Large or complex builds** can consume hundreds or even thousands of credits, depending on the scope of your prompts, the number of files generated, and the iterations required. Before diving in, it helps to **budget for the work ahead**.

### Quick estimation tips

- **Start small**: Build a minimal version of one feature first, note the credit cost, then extrapolate for additional features.
- **Review past builds**: Check your billing history or workspace logs to see how many credits similar prompts consumed.
- **Ask in smaller chunks**: Breaking a big request into multiple focused prompts often gives you better control and visibility into incremental costs.

<Tip title="Test with a prototype">
If you're unsure how expensive a new idea will be, scaffold a simple proof-of-concept in a separate app. Once you've validated the cost and feasibility, you can commit to the full build with confidence.
</Tip>

### When to top up in advance

If you're planning a **major refactor**, **adding a complex backend integration**, or **converting between web and mobile** (see [Web ↔ Mobile conversion](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical)), consider topping up your account beforehand. Running out mid-build can disrupt agent context and require you to re-explain requirements.

For ongoing projects, many users find that **enabling auto-renewal** and setting a comfortable monthly credit allowance provides the smoothest experience—no interruptions, and you stay in flow.
